# Forensic Dossier — freenet AG (FNTN.DE)

*A deep dive on management and the setup. Communication Services / German mobile-and-TV reseller. Eight consecutive quarterly calls reviewed (Q1 2024 through the preliminary full-year 2025 call on 2026-02-26), cross-checked against the screener's hard financials.*

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

freenet is a German "service provider" — it resells mobile capacity it buys from the three network owners (Telekom, Vodafone, Telefónica/O2) rather than owning a network itself, and it runs a fast-growing internet-TV business, waipu.tv, alongside a slowly dying terrestrial-TV stub (freenet TV) and a media-broadcast unit. Across these eight quarters the story moves through three distinct chapters.

**Chapter one — "boring is good" (2024).** Under long-time chief executive Christoph Vilanek the message was deliberately dull: mobile is mature and stable, ARPU (average revenue per user) holds, and the single exciting engine is waipu.tv, which was setting record subscriber adds (close to 139,000 net adds in Q1 2024, up almost 60% year on year) on heavy content and marketing spend. Management was candid about the cost: "the EBITDA is a bit below the previous year… part of the seasonality" (Q1 2024). They also cleanly euthanised a losing unit, closing the Gravis Apple-reseller shops, and signed long-term network contracts they framed as a planning win.

**Chapter two — proof-of-profit and a CEO handover (2025).** The 2024 record-year call (March 2025) pivoted the waipu story from "can it grow?" to "can it pay?" — Vilanek's stated 2025 goal was that waipu "will contribute significantly to our EBITDA," and the year delivered roughly EUR 36 million of adjusted profit from that unit. The dividend was lifted to a proposed EUR 2.07 and a buyback of up to EUR 100 million was floated. Vilanek departed mid-2025 after sixteen years; Robin Harries took over with a more operational, "AI-first telco," churn-reduction, marketing-efficiency vocabulary.

**Chapter three — the contract shock and the value-unlock pivot (late 2025 → early 2026).** Two new threads dominate. First, a damaging admission: one of the network-supply contracts signed in 2024 is now described by the new CEO as a "sick agreement" that could cost up to EUR 50 million of EBITDA across 2026-2028. Second, two value-crystallising moves outside the eight-call window but confirmed live: freenet is monetising its long-held CECONOMY (Media-Markt/Saturn parent) stake into JD.com's takeover, and it has openly begun exploring a stock-market listing of waipu.tv. The narrative has quietly shifted from "operate a stable cash machine" to "surface the hidden assets."

A growth driver that was *added*: the mobilezone acquisition (a German rival distributor closing ~1 million contracts a year), debt-financed. A driver *quietly downgraded*: the personal "2 million waipu subscribers by end-2024" ambition was missed (landed ~1.94 million) and re-based.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | What the numbers say | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Record year 2024… record EBITDA" (Mar-2025) | Net income jumped to EUR 247M (2024) from EUR 155M (2023); EPS EUR 2.08. But adjusted EBITDA was only "stable" without a one-off sale of IP addresses — the CFO admitted this. | Richer in headline than in substance; the record leaned on a one-time asset sale. |
| Revenue is "stable" | Revenue has gently *declined*: EUR 2.63B (2023) → EUR 2.48B (2024) → EUR 2.44B (2025), about -1.5% a year. The scan shows -1.5% year-on-year and a -1.5% three-year growth rate. | Slightly poorer than "stable" — it is a slow fade, masked at the gross-profit line by mix shift to higher-margin service revenue. |
| waipu.tv "getting more and more profitable" | Corroborated: ~EUR 36M adjusted EBITDA contribution in 2025, up from a small positive in 2024, on ~1.94M subscribers. | Matches — the one genuinely strengthening leg. |
| Strong cash generation / capital return | Free cash flow is real: trailing-twelve-month free cash flow EUR 344M, free-cash-flow margin ~14.9%, price-to-free-cash-flow only ~7.1x. Dividend raised to EUR 2.07; ~EUR 60M of the up-to-EUR 100M buyback executed by late 2025. | Matches — the cash story is the backbone of the value case. |
| Earnings reliably delivered | The scan flags a *poor* beat rate: just 1 of the last 7 quarters beat (14%), and the latest quarter's EPS fell ~17% year on year. EBITDA has repeatedly come in "a bit below consensus" by management's own words. | Diverges — they hit full-year guidance but routinely disappoint the quarterly bar; this is a sandbag-the-quarter, defend-the-year pattern. |
| Leverage "already low" | Net debt is real and rising with mobilezone: the live balance-sheet read is EUR 596M net debt (EUR 694M total debt minus EUR 98M cash), financed partly by a bridge loan. Altman-Z solvency score 2.2 sits in the grey zone. | Honest but the trajectory is up, not down. |

The throughline: the **cash and the hidden assets are real; the operating top line is in slow structural decline; and the quarterly earnings quality is weaker than the full-year framing implies.**

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Trajectory: **Declining then re-setting** — confident-but-defensive.

- **Q1 2024 (Vilanek):** offensive, relaxed — "everything on plan and a bit boring… I'm happy that it's true."
- **Mar 2025 (Vilanek, record year):** peak confidence — invents flattering per-employee and per-shop-day cash metrics, "I personally believe in the 2.3 million and… the 3.5 million."
- **May 2025 (Vilanek's last call):** more defensive — "we have, therefore, consequently taken out money of the market… we did on purpose take down the numbers a little bit." Growth is now being *chosen down* to protect price.
- **Nov 2025 (Harries):** energetic but vaguer — heavy on "AI-first," "50 initiatives," "good vibe, good spirit," lighter on hard numbers.
- **Feb 2026 (Harries):** the most defensive of all — leads with what they are "not happy about" (the network contract), frames the year as a fight to "increase prices" against base-churn drag.

The language has clearly migrated from offensive (growth, investment) to defensive (efficiency, churn, price discipline, contract repair). New-CEO calls trade specific numeric guidance for initiative-counting — a yellow flag for guidance precision even as overall candour stays high.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**Reliability: Medium.**

The pattern is consistent: management hits or modestly beats the *full-year* EBITDA guide while letting individual quarters land "a bit below consensus." Full-year 2024 EBITDA guidance was confirmed all year and delivered; 2025 guidance was confirmed at every call and the year closed on plan with the record dividend. That is genuine multi-year reliability.

Against it: the screener's 14% quarterly beat rate, the missed personal "2 million by 2024" waipu target, the serially-extended buyback ("up to EUR 100 million" that mostly stopped at ~EUR 60M), and — most seriously — the *fact that the damaging 2024 network contract was signed by this same team and only re-disclosed as a "sick agreement" two years later*. They are honest in hindsight but the contract was a self-inflicted forecasting miss. Net: trust the full-year guide, discount the quarterly colour and the longer-dated "ambitions."

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **The network-supply contract.** Joshua Mills (BNP Paribas, Feb-2026) pressed hard on freenet's legal leverage to force better tariffs out of the network owner. Management refused to detail it — "I do not want to talk about it… we see possibilities there" — and even declined to confirm the contract's end date. This deflection sits on top of a EUR 50M EBITDA hole; it is the single least-answered question on the calls.
- **waipu net-add deceleration.** Analysts repeatedly probed whether slowing adds reflect market fatigue. Management leaned on the O2/Telefónica churn adjustment to explain the optics and re-based the 2028 target to ~3 million.
- **Capital allocation / buyback follow-through.** Simon Stippig (Warburg) asked across multiple calls whether the full EUR 100M buyback would be executed; the answer kept softening to "we'll decide based on cash development."
- **The CECONOMY stake.** Asked about it in 2025, Vilanek insisted "we would be the last one to give away our shares" — then the company committed to tender into JD.com's bid. The stance reversed, validating analyst suspicion that the stake was monetisable.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

🔴 The 2024 network contract is a self-inflicted, up-to-EUR 50M EBITDA wound across 2026-2028, with no disclosed legal remedy and management dodging the leverage question (Feb-2026).
🔴 Revenue is in slow structural decline (-1.5%/yr) and the latest quarter's EPS fell ~17% year on year; the "record 2024" leaned on a one-off IP-address sale.
🔴 Net debt rose to ~EUR 596M on the bridge-financed mobilezone deal; Altman-Z 2.2 is grey-zone; quarterly beat rate just 14%.
🔴 Buyback follow-through softened; longer-dated "ambitions" (2M waipu) have already missed once.

🟢 waipu.tv is a genuine, growing, now-profitable internet-TV winner (~EUR 36M EBITDA, ~1.94M subs) — and management has begun a process to surface its value via a possible listing.
🟢 Cash conversion is excellent: ~EUR 344M trailing free cash flow at ~7.1x price-to-free-cash-flow, funding a ~EUR 2.07 dividend.
🟢 The CECONOMY stake is being monetised into JD.com's EUR 4.60/share cash bid — a real, near-term cash inflow (~EUR 150M expected in the first half of 2026).
🟢 Management showed discipline closing the loss-making Gravis unit and is choosing margin over volume in mobile ("quality over quantity").

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- **Vocabulary swap with the CEO change.** Vilanek spoke the language of an operator-salesman ("acquisition machines," "fishing in the same pot"); Harries speaks the language of a transformation programme ("AI-first telco," "return on ad spend," "50 churn initiatives"). The substance underneath is the same asset-light reseller — watch that the AI talk does not become a substitute for the missing tariff fix.
- **From "strategic forever-holder" to seller.** The CECONOMY about-face (2025 "last to sell" → 2026 tendering) and the waipu "strategic options / possible IPO" announcement together mark a real strategic shift toward crystallising hidden value — the most important new signal in the file.
- **Mobile growth is now being throttled on purpose.** "We took out money out of the market… we did on purpose take down the numbers" (May-2025) means headline subscriber growth understates the franchise; the lever is price, not weakness.
- **1&1 partnership as incremental, not substitution.** The new 1&1 reselling deal is framed carefully as *incremental* sales — a tell that management knows analysts fear channel cannibalisation.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Classification: STABLE, tilting toward value-unlock.**

This is an asset-light, cash-rich German reseller whose core is in slow managed decline but which sits on two under-appreciated assets — a growing, newly-profitable internet-TV business (waipu) and a soon-to-be-cash CECONOMY stake — and whose new management has visibly begun to surface them. The single most important thing the director must weigh before sizing: **the load-bearing upside is the waipu.tv listing, which is a soft, non-binding "strategic option" with no fixed date and no commitment to reduce the majority stake — so the sum-of-the-parts discount is real but its realisation timing is uncertain, while the EUR 50M network-contract drag is a near-certain, dated EBITDA headwind that bites first.** Size to the cash-and-CECONOMY floor, treat the waipu listing as the optionality, not the base case.

**Economic moat — NARROW, STABLE.** The moat type is a blend of intangible-brand and modest switching-cost in a regulated reseller niche. The returns evidence supports "narrow but real, not eroding": return on invested capital 10.7%, return on equity 12.5%, net margin 11.1% (roughly stable), gross margin ~26% (stable) and *rising* at the group gross-profit line on mix. These are solid for an asset-light model and are not collapsing — so this is a narrow moat holding its width, not an eroding one. The genuine structural threat is confined to the small, openly-declining terrestrial freenet-TV stub (a cord-cutting / linear-media tail) — but that unit is a shrinking minority of profit, and waipu is the *winning* side of the same streaming shift. The cheapness is therefore best read as a fear-print and a conglomerate-discount mispricing, not a melting terminal value.

# Forensic Dossier — freenet AG (FNTN.DE)

*A deep dive on management and the setup. Communication Services / German mobile-and-TV reseller. Eight consecutive quarterly calls reviewed (Q1 2024 through the preliminary full-year 2025 call on 2026-02-26), cross-checked against the screener's hard financials.*

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

freenet is a German "service provider" — it resells mobile capacity it buys from the three network owners (Telekom, Vodafone, Telefónica/O2) rather than owning a network itself, and it runs a fast-growing internet-TV business, waipu.tv, alongside a slowly dying terrestrial-TV stub (freenet TV) and a media-broadcast unit. Across these eight quarters the story moves through three distinct chapters.

**Chapter one — "boring is good" (2024).** Under long-time chief executive Christoph Vilanek the message was deliberately dull: mobile is mature and stable, ARPU (average revenue per user) holds, and the single exciting engine is waipu.tv, which was setting record subscriber adds (close to 139,000 net adds in Q1 2024, up almost 60% year on year) on heavy content and marketing spend. Management was candid about the cost: "the EBITDA is a bit below the previous year… part of the seasonality" (Q1 2024). They also cleanly euthanised a losing unit, closing the Gravis Apple-reseller shops, and signed long-term network contracts they framed as a planning win.

**Chapter two — proof-of-profit and a CEO handover (2025).** The 2024 record-year call (March 2025) pivoted the waipu story from "can it grow?" to "can it pay?" — Vilanek's stated 2025 goal was that waipu "will contribute significantly to our EBITDA," and the year delivered roughly EUR 36 million of adjusted profit from that unit. The dividend was lifted to a proposed EUR 2.07 and a buyback of up to EUR 100 million was floated. Vilanek departed mid-2025 after sixteen years; Robin Harries took over with a more operational, "AI-first telco," churn-reduction, marketing-efficiency vocabulary.

**Chapter three — the contract shock and the value-unlock pivot (late 2025 → early 2026).** Two new threads dominate. First, a damaging admission: one of the network-supply contracts signed in 2024 is now described by the new CEO as a "sick agreement" that could cost up to EUR 50 million of EBITDA across 2026-2028. Second, two value-crystallising moves outside the eight-call window but confirmed live: freenet is monetising its long-held CECONOMY (Media-Markt/Saturn parent) stake into JD.com's takeover, and it has openly begun exploring a stock-market listing of waipu.tv. The narrative has quietly shifted from "operate a stable cash machine" to "surface the hidden assets."

A growth driver that was *added*: the mobilezone acquisition (a German rival distributor closing ~1 million contracts a year), debt-financed. A driver *quietly downgraded*: the personal "2 million waipu subscribers by end-2024" ambition was missed (landed ~1.94 million) and re-based.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | What the numbers say | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Record year 2024… record EBITDA" (Mar-2025) | Net income jumped to EUR 247M (2024) from EUR 155M (2023); EPS EUR 2.08. But adjusted EBITDA was only "stable" without a one-off sale of IP addresses — the CFO admitted this. | Richer in headline than in substance; the record leaned on a one-time asset sale. |
| Revenue is "stable" | Revenue has gently *declined*: EUR 2.63B (2023) → EUR 2.48B (2024) → EUR 2.44B (2025), about -1.5% a year. The scan shows -1.5% year-on-year and a -1.5% three-year growth rate. | Slightly poorer than "stable" — it is a slow fade, masked at the gross-profit line by mix shift to higher-margin service revenue. |

Dividend raised to EUR 2.07; ~EUR 60M of the up-to-EUR 100M buyback executed by late 2025. | Matches — the cash story is the backbone of the value case. |

EBITDA has repeatedly come in "a bit below consensus" by management's own words. | Diverges — they hit full-year guidance but routinely disappoint the quarterly bar; this is a sandbag-the-quarter, defend-the-year pattern. |

The throughline: the **cash and the hidden assets are real; the operating top line is in slow structural decline; and the quarterly earnings quality is weaker than the full-year framing implies.**

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Trajectory: **Declining then re-setting** — confident-but-defensive.

- **Q1 2024 (Vilanek):** offensive, relaxed — "everything on plan and a bit boring… I'm happy that it's true."
- **Mar 2025 (Vilanek, record year):** peak confidence — invents flattering per-employee and per-shop-day cash metrics, "I personally believe in the 2.3 million and… the 3.5 million."
- **May 2025 (Vilanek's last call):** more defensive — "we have, therefore, consequently taken out money of the market… we did on purpose take down the numbers a little bit." Growth is now being *chosen down* to protect price.
- **Nov 2025 (Harries):** energetic but vaguer — heavy on "AI-first," "50 initiatives," "good vibe, good spirit," lighter on hard numbers.
- **Feb 2026 (Harries):** the most defensive of all — leads with what they are "not happy about" (the network contract), frames the year as a fight to "increase prices" against base-churn drag.

The language has clearly migrated from offensive (growth, investment) to defensive (efficiency, churn, price discipline, contract repair). New-CEO calls trade specific numeric guidance for initiative-counting — a yellow flag for guidance precision even as overall candour stays high.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**Reliability: Medium.**

The pattern is consistent: management hits or modestly beats the *full-year* EBITDA guide while letting individual quarters land "a bit below consensus." Full-year 2024 EBITDA guidance was confirmed all year and delivered; 2025 guidance was confirmed at every call and the year closed on plan with the record dividend. That is genuine multi-year reliability.

Against it: the screener's 14% quarterly beat rate, the missed personal "2 million by 2024" waipu target, the serially-extended buyback ("up to EUR 100 million" that mostly stopped at ~EUR 60M), and — most seriously — the *fact that the damaging 2024 network contract was signed by this same team and only re-disclosed as a "sick agreement" two years later*. They are honest in hindsight but the contract was a self-inflicted forecasting miss. Net: trust the full-year guide, discount the quarterly colour and the longer-dated "ambitions."

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **The network-supply contract.** Joshua Mills (BNP Paribas, Feb-2026) pressed hard on freenet's legal leverage to force better tariffs out of the network owner. Management refused to detail it — "I do not want to talk about it… we see possibilities there" — and even declined to confirm the contract's end date. This deflection sits on top of a EUR 50M EBITDA hole; it is the single least-answered question on the calls.
- **waipu net-add deceleration.** Analysts repeatedly probed whether slowing adds reflect market fatigue. Management leaned on the O2/Telefónica churn adjustment to explain the optics and re-based the 2028 target to ~3 million.
- **Capital allocation / buyback follow-through.** Simon Stippig (Warburg) asked across multiple calls whether the full EUR 100M buyback would be executed; the answer kept softening to "we'll decide based on cash development."
- **The CECONOMY stake.** Asked about it in 2025, Vilanek insisted "we would be the last one to give away our shares" — then the company committed to tender into JD.com's bid. The stance reversed, validating analyst suspicion that the stake was monetisable.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

🔴 The 2024 network contract is a self-inflicted, up-to-EUR 50M EBITDA wound across 2026-2028, with no disclosed legal remedy and management dodging the leverage question (Feb-2026).
🔴 Revenue is in slow structural decline (-1.5%/yr) and the latest quarter's EPS fell ~17% year on year; the "record 2024" leaned on a one-off IP-address sale.
🔴 Net debt rose to ~EUR 596M on the bridge-financed mobilezone deal; Altman-Z 2.2 is grey-zone; quarterly beat rate just 14%.
🔴 Buyback follow-through softened; longer-dated "ambitions" (2M waipu) have already missed once.

🟢 waipu.tv is a genuine, growing, now-profitable internet-TV winner (~EUR 36M EBITDA, ~1.94M subs) — and management has begun a process to surface its value via a possible listing.
🟢 Cash conversion is excellent: ~EUR 344M trailing free cash flow at ~7.1x price-to-free-cash-flow, funding a ~EUR 2.07 dividend.
🟢 The CECONOMY stake is being monetised into JD.com's EUR 4.60/share cash bid — a real, near-term cash inflow (~EUR 150M expected in the first half of 2026).
🟢 Management showed discipline closing the loss-making Gravis unit and is choosing margin over volume in mobile ("quality over quantity").

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- **Vocabulary swap with the CEO change.** Vilanek spoke the language of an operator-salesman ("acquisition machines," "fishing in the same pot"); Harries speaks the language of a transformation programme ("AI-first telco," "return on ad spend," "50 churn initiatives"). The substance underneath is the same asset-light reseller — watch that the AI talk does not become a substitute for the missing tariff fix.
- **From "strategic forever-holder" to seller.** The CECONOMY about-face (2025 "last to sell" → 2026 tendering) and the waipu "strategic options / possible IPO" announcement together mark a real strategic shift toward crystallising hidden value — the most important new signal in the file.
- **Mobile growth is now being throttled on purpose.** "We took out money out of the market… we did on purpose take down the numbers" (May-2025) means headline subscriber growth understates the franchise; the lever is price, not weakness.
- **1&1 partnership as incremental, not substitution.** The new 1&1 reselling deal is framed carefully as *incremental* sales — a tell that management knows analysts fear channel cannibalisation.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Classification: STABLE, tilting toward value-unlock.**

This is an asset-light, cash-rich German reseller whose core is in slow managed decline but which sits on two under-appreciated assets — a growing, newly-profitable internet-TV business (waipu) and a soon-to-be-cash CECONOMY stake — and whose new management has visibly begun to surface them. The single most important thing the director must weigh before sizing: **the load-bearing upside is the waipu.tv listing, which is a soft, non-binding "strategic option" with no fixed date and no commitment to reduce the majority stake — so the sum-of-the-parts discount is real but its realisation timing is uncertain, while the EUR 50M network-contract drag is a near-certain, dated EBITDA headwind that bites first.** Size to the cash-and-CECONOMY floor, treat the waipu listing as the optionality, not the base case.

**Economic moat — NARROW, STABLE.** The moat type is a blend of intangible-brand and modest switching-cost in a regulated reseller niche. The returns evidence supports "narrow but real, not eroding": return on invested capital 10.7%, return on equity 12.5%, net margin 11.1% (roughly stable), gross margin ~26% (stable) and *rising* at the group gross-profit line on mix. These are solid for an asset-light model and are not collapsing — so this is a narrow moat holding its width, not an eroding one. The genuine structural threat is confined to the small, openly-declining terrestrial freenet-TV stub (a cord-cutting / linear-media tail) — but that unit is a shrinking minority of profit, and waipu is the *winning* side of the same streaming shift. The cheapness is therefore best read as a fear-print and a conglomerate-discount mispricing, not a melting terminal value.

The multi-year ambition was a clean, oft-repeated target: €600 million of EBITDA by 2028, with waipu.tv reaching 3.5 million subscribers.

# Forensic Dossier — freenet AG (FNTN.DE)

*A deep dive on management and the setup, prepared for the investment committee. freenet is Germany's largest independent mobile-service reseller — it sells mobile plans that run over other companies' networks (a mobile virtual network operator, or MVNO) rather than owning towers itself — plus a fast-growing internet-TV business, waipu.tv, and a shrinking legacy broadcast unit. The transcripts span Q1 2024 through the preliminary full-year 2025 call (February 2026), across a CEO handover from Christoph Vilanek to Robin Harries.*

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story management told changed materially over these two years, and not in the company's favor.

Through 2024 and into early 2025, the arc was confident and offensive. Long-time CEO Christoph Vilanek framed 2024 as a "record year" — record earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) of €521.5 million, record postpaid mobile net additions, and a waipu.tv internet-TV business finally crossing from "great product, but can it make money?" into real profit contribution. The capital-return message was generous and specific: a dividend raised to €1.97, an 80%-of-free-cash-flow payout policy, and a share buyback of "up to €100 million." The multi-year ambition was a clean, oft-repeated target: €600 million of EBITDA by 2028, with waipu.tv reaching 3.5 million subscribers.

By the November 2025 and February 2026 calls, under new CEO Robin Harries, the tone shifted from harvesting a mature business to defending and rebuilding it. Three narrative threads appeared that were absent at the start: (1) an "AI-first telco" transformation and a "customer value management" churn-reduction project — over 50 initiatives, an AI voice bot, elasticity testing — which is the language of a company that needs to fix its retention, not one coasting on a moat; (2) the €340 million mobilezone acquisition (a direct competitor bought to add sales scale and Apple-procurement channels); and (3) the single most important disclosure in the entire transcript set — a network-operator contract signed in 2024 that management now admits could cost "up to EUR 50 million negative EBITDA impact for the year '26 to '28."

The waipu.tv subscriber ambition also quietly contracted. The old "2 million by end of 2024 / 2.3 million by end of 2025" targets were missed (1.94 million at end-2024, and management conceded it "missed my personal ambition of 2 million"), then re-based after stripping out a Telefónica ("O2") sub-base cleanup to 1.755 million. The 2024 EBITDA record leaned partly on a one-off sale of internet-protocol (IP) addresses, which management itself flagged. |

The terminology migration is telling: from Vilanek's "acquisition machine" and "record" (offense) to Harries's "lean, focused, effective," "customer value management," and "AI-first" (defense/efficiency). **Classification: DETERIORATING** (operationally), atop a genuinely cheap and cash-generative base. This is a deep-value, mature-telecom-reseller situation — not a growth story. # Forensic Dossier — freenet AG (FNTN.DE)

*A deep dive on management and the setup, prepared for the investment committee. freenet is Germany's largest independent mobile-service reseller — it sells mobile plans that run over other companies' networks (a mobile virtual network operator, or MVNO) rather than owning towers itself — plus a fast-growing internet-TV business, waipu.tv, and a shrinking legacy broadcast unit. The transcripts span Q1 2024 through the preliminary full-year 2025 call (February 2026), across a CEO handover from Christoph Vilanek to Robin Harries.*

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story management told changed materially over these two years, and not in the company's favor.

Through 2024 and into early 2025, the arc was confident and offensive. Long-time CEO Christoph Vilanek framed 2024 as a "record year" — record earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) of €521.5 million, record postpaid mobile net additions, and a waipu.tv internet-TV business finally crossing from "great product, but can it make money?" into real profit contribution. The capital-return message was generous and specific: a dividend raised to €1.97, an 80%-of-free-cash-flow payout policy, and a share buyback of "up to €100 million." The multi-year ambition was a clean, oft-repeated target: €600 million of EBITDA by 2028, with waipu.tv reaching 3.5 million subscribers.

By the November 2025 and February 2026 calls, under new CEO Robin Harries, the tone shifted from harvesting a mature business to defending and rebuilding it. Three narrative threads appeared that were absent at the start: (1) an "AI-first telco" transformation and a "customer value management" churn-reduction project — over 50 initiatives, an AI voice bot, elasticity testing — which is the language of a company that needs to fix its retention, not one coasting on a moat; (2) the €340 million mobilezone acquisition (a direct competitor bought to add sales scale and Apple-procurement channels); and (3) the single most important disclosure in the entire transcript set — a network-operator contract signed in 2024 that management now admits could cost "up to EUR 50 million negative EBITDA impact for the year '26 to '28."

The waipu.tv subscriber ambition also quietly contracted. The old "2 million by end of 2024 / 2.3 million by end of 2025" targets were missed (1.94 million at end-2024, and management conceded it "missed my personal ambition of 2 million"), then re-based after stripping out a Telefónica ("O2") sub-base cleanup to 1.755 million. The 2028 target of ~3 million was reaffirmed, but only after the goalposts moved.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | The actual numbers | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Record year 2024," EBITDA €521.5M | Net income did climb impressively — 2022 €79M → 2023 €155M → 2024 €247M → 2025 €271M; earnings per share €0.67 → €2.30. But revenue is *falling*: €2.63B (2023) → €2.48B (2024) → €2.44B (2025), −1.5% last year. | Mixed — profit growth is real, but it is a shrinking-top-line, margin-and-buyback story, not a growth story. The 2024 EBITDA record leaned partly on a one-off sale of internet-protocol (IP) addresses, which management itself flagged. |
| waipu.tv "will contribute significantly to EBITDA" | Confirmed: ~€36 million adjusted EBITDA from waipu.tv in 2025, up from a slim contribution in 2024. | Verified — this is the one clearly delivered promise. |
| "Fully confirmed" guidance, repeatedly | Yet the earnings-beat record is poor: management beat consensus in only 1 of the last 7 quarters (14%). The latest quarter's EPS fell 17% year over year. | Poor — the "everything on plan, a bit boring" self-image is contradicted by a 14% beat rate and a Q4 2025 miss that sank the shares ~11%. |
| Strong capital returns (dividend + buyback) | Dividend raised to €2.07; trailing free cash flow €344 million (TTM) supports it. But net debt sits at ~€596M (total debt €694M less €98M cash), lifted by the €340M mobilezone deal financed with a bridge loan. | Real but now leveraged — the balance sheet is no longer the pristine "0.5× net-debt/EBITDA" management cited; the buyback was capped at ~€60M, not the "up to €100M" headline. |
| Price/free-cash-flow ~7×, margin of safety across models | P/FCF ~7.0×, and internal models (discounted cash flow, earnings-power value, Graham, owner-earnings) show +35% to +63% margins of safety. Return on invested capital 10.7%, net margin 11.1%. | Genuinely cheap on cash-flow — the value signal is not fabricated. The question the financials cannot answer is whether the earnings base is stable or eroding. |

The core divergence: management narrates momentum ("record," "all-time high net adds," "on track for 2028"), while the trajectory is a *flat-to-declining revenue base with rising leverage and a freshly disclosed multi-year EBITDA headwind.* The earnings-per-share growth is real but increasingly manufactured by share count reduction and cost discipline, not organic demand.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Declining.** The confidence peak is Vilanek's March 2025 "record year" farewell — expansive, anecdote-rich, congratulated by analysts on his way out. By February 2026, Harries opens the call by naming what the company is "not happy about" — the network-operator contract — within his first three sentences. The language shifted from offensive (growth, investment, "acquisition machine") to defensive and remedial ("more lean, focused and effective," "churn reduction," "quality over quantity," "we started to increase prices"). The repeated invocation of an "AI-first telco" and "50 initiatives" is the vocabulary of a turnaround, not a compounder. Guidance specificity actually *decreased* on the thing that matters most: the €50M contract hit is framed as a range ("up to") with an unpredictable renegotiation outcome.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**Medium-to-Low.** The 2028 €600M EBITDA ambition has been reaffirmed at every call, which reads as steadiness — but the chief financial officer conceded in November 2025 that "earlier or later… we have to recalculate the levels" and expects to revise the 2028 guide sometime in 2026. Combined with a 14% earnings-beat rate and a waipu.tv target that was quietly re-based, the pattern is one of a management team that sets round-number aspirations and defends them verbally while the sub-components drift. There is no sandbagging pattern (a company that beats consensus only 14% of the time is not lowballing). Reliability: Medium at best, and trending lower as the contract dispute clouds the 2026–2028 bridge.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

Analysts circled the same three sore spots repeatedly. First, the **network-operator (Telefónica) contract**: BNP Paribas's Joshua Mills pressed hard in February 2026 on exactly what legal or contractual leverage freenet has to force better tariffs — and management pointedly declined to answer ("I do not want to talk about" legal options), while also refusing to confirm when the contract expires ("I have not said that it ends in '28"). That evasiveness on the single largest risk is the loudest signal in the transcripts. Second, **waipu.tv net-add deceleration** and whether the entry-level, lower-price "start-up package" is buying growth at the expense of average revenue per user. Third, **the CECONOMY stake** and whether/when the ~€150M of proceeds arrive — management repeatedly deferred. The through-line: on every genuinely load-bearing question, management asked for patience rather than giving specifics.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

🔴 A network-operator contract signed in 2024 that management now admits could cost up to €50M of EBITDA a year through 2028 — self-inflicted, and disclosed only after the fact.
🔴 Management refused to state the contract's expiry or its legal leverage when pressed directly (Feb 2026) — evasive on the biggest risk.
🔴 Revenue has fallen three years running; earnings-per-share growth is increasingly buyback- and cost-driven, not organic.
🔴 The 2024 "record EBITDA" leaned on a one-off IP-address sale, flagged by the CFO himself.
🔴 Net debt rose to ~€596M after the debt-financed mobilezone deal; the buyback was trimmed to ~€60M from the "up to €100M" headline.
🔴 A full CEO handover mid-story — narrative discontinuity at exactly the moment the business turned defensive.

🟢 waipu.tv delivered the promised profit inflection — ~€36M adjusted EBITDA in 2025 — and holds a strong ~20–25% share of a growing German internet-TV market.
🟢 Record postpaid mobile net adds (306,000 organic + 240,000 from mobilezone in 2025); the mobilezone deal adds real sales scale and cleared antitrust.
🟢 Free cash flow is robust (€344M TTM) and the ~7× price/free-cash-flow multiple with a well-covered ~9% dividend yield gives a genuine valuation cushion.
🟢 Management is at least *acting* on churn and pricing (price increases held through Cyber Week 2025) rather than denying the problem.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

The terminology migration is telling: from Vilanek's "acquisition machine" and "record" (offense) to Harries's "lean, focused, effective," "customer value management," and "AI-first" (defense/efficiency). The competitive framing also changed — early calls dismissed cable and housing-association channels as beneath freenet; late calls emphasize *partnering* with former rival 1&1 and buying competitor mobilezone, i.e., consolidation as survival in a saturating market. Most subtly, the shift from "we can grow" to "quality over quantity… we started to increase prices" is an admission that the volume-growth engine has stalled and the lever now is price and retention — a mature-utility posture dressed in growth language.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Classification: DETERIORATING** (operationally), atop a genuinely cheap and cash-generative base. This is a deep-value, mature-telecom-reseller situation — not a growth story. The single most important thing the director must weigh before sizing: **the bad news has largely already happened.** The €50M contract headwind, the weak 2026 guide, and the waipu.tv slowdown drove an approximately 29% share-price collapse into this level; the load-bearing forward catalysts (a Telefónica renegotiation, the CECONOMY cash-out, a possible waipu.tv carve-out) are soft, non-binding, and outside freenet's unilateral control. The valuation cushion is real; the question is whether it compensates for an eroding, price-taking MVNO economic model with no network of its own.

On the **economic moat**: NARROW and ERODING. freenet's edge is an intangible-brand and distribution-scale advantage (Germany's largest independent mobile retailer, ~500–1,000 stores, strong waipu.tv brand), not a durable structural moat — it owns no spectrum and no network, so its mobile economics are ultimately dictated by the three network owners it resells for. Return on invested capital (~10.7%) and return on equity (~12.5%) are moderate, not fortress-like, and the newly disclosed contract shows exactly how the network owners can squeeze the reseller's margin at will. Gross margin is stable (~26% company-wide) but the network-operator dispute is direct evidence of margin capture *by the counterparty*. The **secular threat is material, not terminal**: the German MVNO/mobile market is saturating (management's own "market fatigue" language), and freenet's dependence on network owners is a structural vulnerability — but this is a slow squeeze on a still-cash-generative, dividend-paying base, offset by a genuinely growing internet-TV franchise, not an imminent terminal impairment. The cheapness is closer to a fear-print on already-disclosed bad news than a melting-ice-cube value trap, but the margin of safety must be underwritten as *stable-to-slowly-eroding earnings*, not growth.

# Forensic Dossier — freenet AG (FNTN.DE)

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story management told changed materially over these two years, and not in the company's favor.

Through 2024 and into early 2025, the arc was confident and offensive. Long-time CEO Christoph Vilanek framed 2024 as a "record year" — record earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) of €521.5 million, record postpaid mobile net additions, and a waipu.tv internet-TV business finally crossing from "great product, but can it make money?" into real profit contribution. The multi-year ambition was a clean, oft-repeated target: €600 million of EBITDA by 2028, with waipu.tv reaching 3.5 million subscribers.

By the November 2025 and February 2026 calls, under new CEO Robin Harries, the tone shifted from harvesting a mature business to defending and rebuilding it. Three narrative threads appeared that were absent at the start: (1) an "AI-first telco" transformation and a "customer value management" churn-reduction project — over 50 initiatives, an AI voice bot, elasticity testing — which is the language of a company that needs to fix its retention, not one coasting on a moat; (2) the €340 million mobilezone acquisition (a direct competitor bought to add sales scale and Apple-procurement channels); and (3) the single most important disclosure in the entire transcript set — a network-operator contract signed in 2024 that management now admits could cost "up to EUR 50 million negative EBITDA impact for the year '26 to '28."
